tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

content.text:
We need to map out the page structure with a skip link, header, main content area, and footer, using a hero section with a full-screen photo background from the latest tournament or the default hero image, with a gradient overlay; the hero should display the main heading "История Compass Arena", a subtitle, and statistical highlights like tournaments played, total matches, and team count.Now I'm thinking through the aggregate statistics — I need to count all tournaments and matches across history, plus factor in the current tournament's matches if it's not already archived. The key question is whether the current tournament counts as "held" — I'm working through the logic that if there are no history items, then no tournaments have been completed yet, so the count should reflect that honestly rather than counting an in-progress tournament as held. So the hero section shows a stats row with total finished tournaments, match count, team count, and current champion (or a dash if none). Then there's a "current season" block labeled "Chapter 01" that displays the live tournament status—showing progress based on stats, listing the participating teams, and highlighting the champion if one's been crowned. If there's no history yet, this becomes the only block, with a subtitle explaining it's the opening chapter. If history exists, I'm still rendering the current season card at the top, labeled as the current chapter number.

The key insight is that "current season" is always rendered as the latest chapter, regardless of whether history is empty. The chapter numbering works out: when history is empty, the current season is "Chapter 01" (the only block); when history exists, the current season becomes the last chapter in the sequence. The chapter navigation panel appears only when there are at least two chapters total, including the current one. For each historical item, I'm building out the chapter details with the chapter number, date, name, format, cover image, champion roster, finalist, MVP, and the path to the title.

Now I need to handle the cover image with proper alt text, and I'm noting that within history data, `matches` is separate from `currentSeason` — every item has `teams` and `matches`. The "path to title" for each chapter shows all completed series with round/stage, winner, score, and loser, derived from the history item's own matches. I'll reuse the ladder building logic from the old version but make it more generic since history matches might not follow the old M1–M5 format. For rounds and stages, I'm using `stageLabel` which checks `m.bracket === 'grand'` or `m.id === 5` for the grand final, `m.bracket === 'lower'` for lower bracket, and `m.round === 2` or `m.id === 4` for semifinals. I'll build a function that selects only matches with a winner, sorts by round then id, labels them with stage information, and displays the output in either a grid layout or table format.

For the summary tables, I need to map out champions across all history items — noting that the current season isn't recorded yet until it's finished, so I'll only include history entries. One thing to watch: if the current tournament is already archived in history but not yet marked as complete, I could hit duplicates, so I'll need to handle deduplication if an archived item matches the current tournament.

Now I'm structuring the data: for the champions table, each row shows the chapter number, date, tournament name, champion, finalist, and the grand final score (pulling from either the last match with bracket='grand' and a winner, or the match with id=5). For the clubs and titles table, I'm aggregating across all history items to get titles, finals, matches, and maps per team, plus tracking wins and losses. The MVP showcase section will be a card grid displaying the player nickname, team, tournament, and note — only rendering if at least one MVP exists. Then I need to handle chapter navigation with sticky chips.

I'm also setting up a JSON-LD ItemList for SEO with tournament data from the history plus current season info, and implementing data updates with deduplication to prevent multiple renders in the same frame using requestAnimationFrame. For the lightbox, I'll render its HTML directly in the page markup rather than dynamically inserting it, which keeps things cleaner and uses the existing CSS classes from site.css.

Now I'm checking the lightbox and gallery grid styles to make sure the markup aligns with the existing CSS structure.

content.text:
We need to replace the existing history.html file with a complete rewrite, including the head section with title, metadata, and styles; add the skip link, header, navigation menu, and footer from the index; use the history-specific footer layout with the grid structure, marking "История" in the footer columns.Now I'm setting up the main content structure with a hero section that includes an image, overlay, and chapter navigation, then a container for the chapters and tables, plus a lightbox element for viewing photos. The script will load the history data and inject the sprite and chrome elements, using a sticky chapter navigation panel that highlights the active chapter as you scroll.

I'm thinking about where to place the sticky nav in the DOM — it needs to be outside the hero to work properly when scrolling, positioned after the hero element with the chapters following it. The current season should be the first chapter in the navigation. Let me clarify the numbering scheme: the current season is always the newest entry and gets the highest chapter number, so if the history is empty it becomes chapter 01, and if there are three past tournaments plus the current season, the current season becomes chapter 04. This keeps things chronologically consistent since the archive is ordered from oldest to newest. Now for the hero section background — I need to pull the first photo from the latest archived tournament, or fall back to the hero image.

I'm adding a scrim overlay to the hero background using a container with a media element and shade div, then styling it appropriately. I'm also setting up two data tables: one for champions showing the chapter number, date, tournament name, champion, runner-up, and final score, and another for club titles and achievements displaying club name, titles, finals, matches, and maps. For the second table, I need to aggregate data across all tournaments in the history, including the current season if it has a champion determined. I'll include the current season's champion in the clubs table and in the final score calculation since it's a real sporting result, but exclude incomplete or upcoming seasons since there's no champion yet. This gives a complete picture of all titles won across the organization's history.

For MVP showcases, I'll only include history entries since the current season has no MVP field — that's fine. The MVP chips will link back to their chapter anchors. Now I'm setting up the JSON-LD ItemList structure with tournament data using ItemList and ListItem schema types, where each entry includes the tournament name, date, and champion information with proper URL anchors.

Building the lightbox functionality...

The lightbox needs to handle gallery clicks across all chapters, use keyboard navigation with arrow keys and escape, support swipe gestures on mobile, display the current position counter, and manage body scroll locking. I'll store the photo collections in a registry indexed by chapter so each gallery can retrieve its full set when opened. The gallery structure will include individual photo items with zoom data attributes.

For the gallery markup, I need to set appropriate alt text for images—using captions when available, otherwise falling back to a chapter-based description like "Фото с турнира {name}". The `.g-cap` element already handles caption display, so that stays as-is. I'm aiming for consistency with the project's ES5 style, avoiding template literals.

Now I'm structuring the chapter navigation chips and planning the render flow: loading data, setting up change listeners and auto-refresh, then reinitializing observers and lightbox handlers after each render with proper cleanup. The reveal system observes new elements to add staggered animation classes, the chapter spy watches for navigation updates, and chapter covers get their own observer for the `.in` class to trigger the zoom animation.

For the head progress bar, I'll calculate it as the ratio of played matches to total matches on the current tournament — this gives users a visual indicator of how far along the bracket they are. I'm wrapping the gallery assignment logic in a try-catch to handle environments where querySelectorAll might return a NodeList without forEach support, or where closest() isn't available on targets. For the test harness, I need to ensure the spies and current chapter elements have proper IDs so they can be found, and I'm planning out the smoke-history test scenario.

Writing test harness setup... I need to check how `CA.data.normalize` handles the history array — it's passed through as-is without normalizing the teams and matches within each history item, so test fixtures need to use the normalized structure. The old code accessed `m.round`, `m.score1/2`, `m.winner` directly, and history matches reference team IDs that are only available in the history item's own teams array. Since `CA.data.team()` won't find them, I'll need my own resolver to look up teams by ID within each history item.

Now I'm ready to write the full implementation. Let me first verify the `wrap` layout works with the sticky header offsets, then create the chapter navigation markup with the wrapping div and inner container.

Writing component styles... Adding more styles... Adding more table and styling rules... Adding responsive styles... Building the HTML structure with a hero section, sticky navigation, and content containers, plus a lightbox for the photo viewer. Completing the lightbox markup with the image, caption, and close button, then adding the skip link and progress bar with proper ARIA attributes. I'm also considering whether to preload the hero image like index.html does, though without a picture element I'll keep it simple and skip that for now.

For accessibility, I need to make sure the menu has the right aria attributes and the close button works properly. When the script runs, it'll inject the sprite and initialize the chrome, then load data to render the page. The key thing is that the reveal system only observes elements after they're inserted into the DOM, so I need to call the observe function after the HTML is in place.

Looking at the smoke test timing, I have about 120ms after setup for initialization to complete — the script runs synchronously during DOMContentLoaded, then the fetch resolves as a microtask, so there's plenty of time. The history module attaches its contentReady listener during its own eval, which means it'll be registered before the DOMContentLoaded event actually fires since the DOM is already parsed at that point.

Now I need to handle the `renderChapters` function, which builds the chapter list from the history array and current season, then generates the HTML for each chapter and renders the aggregate tables. I'll also need to convert timestamps like `createdAt` into a human-readable date format.

Writing the chapter rendering logic... Still writing styles...

For the current season status, I'm handling three cases: if it's complete, show "Турнир завершён" with a trophy; if it's live, show "Идёт сейчас" with a live indicator; otherwise show "До старта" with the formatted tournament start date if available.

I'm tracking progress through the matches with a bar showing played versus total matches, or an empty state message if nothing's been played yet. The roster displays team names as chips, and if there's a champion, I'll show that with a trophy. Action buttons link to the bracket and schedule pages.

If there's no history yet, I'm adding a note explaining this is the first chapter and that past tournament archives will appear here once they're completed. I'm also setting up a path-to-title section...

Building the title path component... Building the champion roster... Writing helper functions... Writing getter functions... Writing the tournament stats aggregation... Checking the order of operations in `CA.data.load()` — the finalize call happens before `D.fromServer` is set, which is fine. Now I'm building the current season data object from the loaded dataset with the teams, matches, and computed phase information. Then I'm moving on to structure the HTML for the champions table.

Building the clubs and titles table... Finishing the tournament summary and moving into the MVP showcase section, which maps over all MVPs across tournaments and displays them as cards with links back to their respective chapters.

Now I'm setting up the JSON-LD schema for all tournaments, structuring them as a list of events with their details.

I need to be careful about duplicate IDs when injecting the schema — I'll check if the element already exists and update it rather than creating a new one, so the test harness doesn't end up with multiple instances. The hero stats should pull from the all-time aggregate data, counting the current tournament if it's archived, otherwise just the history entries.

For teams, I'm counting unique team names across all tournaments and the current season. The total matches metric should represent the archive only, not including the ongoing tournament.

Writing the final render function... Writing the render function... Setting up the lightbox initialization to handle image loading, close buttons, navigation arrows, and overlay clicks, plus keyboard and swipe support. Then in the main init, I'm loading the data, rendering, and starting auto-refresh with change listeners.

Now I need to rewrite the HTML file completely. I should keep the existing URL structure from ca-views which uses the `/history.html#ch-<id>` anchor format. For chapter IDs, I'll use `'ch-' + (h.id || index)`. Also need to ensure history entries without a photos array are handled safely by defaulting to an empty array.

Writing the new file...
Now I have the full picture. Let me write the new `history.html`.

/* ==========================================================
   ИСТОРИЯ ТУРНИРОВ

/* ---------- Заглавный экран ---------- */
.h-hero { position: relative; height: 100svh; min-height: 560px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: flex-end; overflow: hidden; }
.h-hero-media { position: absolute; inset: 0; }

.h-hero.in .h-hero-media img { transform: scale(1); }
.h-hero-shade { position: absolute; inset: 0; background:
    linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(7,8,10,.6) 0%, rgba(7,8,10,.15) 32%, rgba(7,8,10,.35) 60%, var(--bg) 100%),
    linear-gradient(0deg, var(--bg), transparent 5%); }
.h-hero-body { position: relative; z-index: 1; padding-bottom: 72px; }
.h-hero .kicker { color: var(--text); opacity: .8; }
.h-hero h1 { font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 300; font-size: clamp(38px, 6.4vw, 92px); line-height: .98; letter-spacing: -.03em; max-width: 16em; }
.h-hero .sub { margin-top: 22px; color: var(--text-2); font-size: clamp(15px, 1.3vw, 18px); max-width: 42em; }
.h-hero-stats { display: flex; gap: clamp(28px, 5vw, 64px); margin-top: 40px; flex-wrap: wrap; }
.h-stat b { display: block; font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 200; font-size: clamp(26px, 3vw, 40px); color: var(--gold-hi); line-height: 1; }
.h-stat span { display: block; font-size: 13px; color: var(--text-3); margin-top: 8px; }
.h-scroll { position: absolute; left: 28px; bottom: 26px; z-index: 1; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; color: var(--text-3); font-size: 12px; letter-spacing: .04em; }
.h-scroll svg { width: 13px; height: 13px; stroke: var(--text-3); animation: bob 2.2s ease-in-out infinite; }
@keyframes bob { 0%,100% { transform: translateY(0); } 50% { transform: translateY(5px); } }

/* ---------- Пустое состояние ---------- */
.h-empty { position: relative; padding-top: 120px; padding-bottom: 160px; text-align: left; overflow: hidden; }
.h-empty::before { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 0; background: radial-gradient(ellipse 60% 50% at 78% 15%, rgba(201,163,90,.10), transparent 65%); }
.h-empty .num-ghost { font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 200; font-size: clamp(120px, 22vw, 320px); line-height: .8; color: transparent; -webkit-text-stroke: 1px var(--line-2); position: absolute; right: -.06em; top: -.08em; pointer-events: none; user-select: none; }
.h-empty-inner { position: relative; max-width: 640px; }
.h-empty h2 { font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 300; font-size: clamp(30px, 4vw, 48px); line-height: 1.12; letter-spacing: -.02em; margin-bottom: 18px; }
.h-empty p { color: var(--text-2); font-size: 16px; max-width: 46ch; margin-bottom: 30px; }

.h-now { position: relative; padding-top: 96px; padding-bottom: 120px; }
.h-now .num-ghost { font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 200; font-size: clamp(140px, 24vw, 340px); line-height: .8; color: transparent; -webkit-text-stroke: 1px var(--line-2); position: absolute; right: 28px; top: 60px; pointer-events: none; user-select: none; }
.h-now-inner { position: relative; max-width: 760px; }
.h-now h2 { font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 300; font-size: clamp(30px, 4.4vw, 56px); line-height: 1.05; letter-spacing: -.02em; margin-bottom: 18px; }
.h-now .lead { margin-bottom: 36px; }
.now-live { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; color: var(--gold-hi); }
.progress { margin: 0 0 36px; max-width: 520px; }
.progress .top { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; font-size: 13.5px; color: var(--text-2); margin-bottom: 12px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
.progress .track { height: 1px; background: var(--line-2); position: relative; }
.progress .track i { position: absolute; left: 0; top: -1px; height: 3px; background: var(--gold); border-radius: 2px; }
.now-teams { margin-bottom: 40px; }
.now-teams .eyebrow { color: var(--text-3); font-size: 12.5px; margin-bottom: 14px; }
.now-champ { margin: 0 0 36px; padding-left: 20px; border-left: 2px solid var(--gold); }
.now-champ small { display: block; color: var(--text-3); font-size: 12.5px; margin-bottom: 6px; }
.now-champ b { font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 400; font-size: clamp(22px, 3vw, 34px); color: var(--gold-hi); }
.now-cta { display: flex; gap: 12px; flex-wrap: wrap; }

/* ---------- Навигация по главам ---------- */
.h-nav { position: sticky; top: var(--head-h); z-index: 40; padding-top: 14px; padding-bottom: 14px; background: linear-gradient(180deg, var(--bg) 60%, transparent); }
.h-nav-inner { display: flex; gap: 8px; overflow-x: auto; scrollbar-width: none; padding: 2px; }
.h-nav-inner::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }
.h-chip { flex: none; height: 36px; padding: 0 16px; border-radius: 999px; border: 1px solid var(--line-2); background: rgba(7,8,10,.7); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(10px); backdrop-filter: blur(10px); color: var(--text-2); font-size: 13px; text-decoration: none; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; transition: color .2s, background .2s, border-color .2s; }
.h-chip:hover { color: var(--text); border-color: rgba(255,255,255,.3); }

.chapter-mark .rule { flex: 1; height: 1px; background: var(--line); }

.chapter-cover { position: relative; border-radius: 22px; overflow: hidden; height: min(74vh, 720px); min-height: 340px; }

.chapter-cover.in img { transform: scale(1); }

.chapter-cover.flat .flat-num { position: absolute; font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 200; font-size: clamp(160px, 24vw, 420px); line-height: 1; color: transparent; -webkit-text-stroke: 1px var(--line-2); user-select: none; }
.cover-caption { position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; padding: clamp(20px, 4vw, 48px); z-index: 1; }
.cc-tag { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; font-size: 12.5px; color: var(--gold-hi); letter-spacing: .06em; margin-bottom: 14px; }

.cover-caption .champ { font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 400; font-size: clamp(26px, 4.2vw, 52px); line-height: 1.05; color: var(--text); }

.roster { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 8px; }

.g-item:hover .g-cap { opacity: 1; }

.lb.active { opacity: 1; visibility: visible; }
.lb-frame { max-width: min(1200px, 92vw); max-height: 82vh; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 16px; }
.lb-frame img { max-width: 100%; max-height: 74vh; border-radius: 8px; object-fit: contain; box-shadow: 0 30px 90px -20px rgba(0,0,0,.6); }
.lb-cap { color: var(--text-2); font-size: 14px; text-align: center; max-width: 60ch; min-height: 1.4em; }

Need to name the main script file `assets/ca-history.js` and create it with a self-contained IIFE that references CA.data, CA.ui, and CA.views at call time rather than initialization, to avoid timing issues with script loading order and ensure the required libraries are loaded first.I'm creating a helper function to safely escape strings, then defining utilities for finding items by id, retrieving photos from the data structure, and formatting dates with a fallback to the createdAt timestamp if the provided date is invalid.

I'm also building alias functions for team lookups within a given data structure and implementing a function that normalizes match state by setting defaults for scores and checking if the match has been played.

Now I'm working on the allTimeStats function that aggregates statistics across all matches, filtering for non-slot team names and skipping invalid entries. I'm building a map to track each team's stats per tournament and overall, then converting it to an array.

Continuing with the team aggregation logic...

Now I'm defining a function that checks if each team should be included, then building a function that generates a stat card HTML element with a value and label. I'm also handling the hero section, which pulls the latest photo from a sorted list or uses a fallback image, with different alt text depending on whether it's from tournament data or just the arena background. Figuring out the hero sub text — if there's a champion, show their name; otherwise, if there are archived tournaments, mention how many have been played and that the current season is underway; if nothing's archived yet, use a different message. The figures grid displays total tournaments, matches, teams, and the current champion, with the champion name using a special text styling to handle long names.

For the current season block, I'm building the markup with an id attribute based on whether we have archived data. The render logic keeps the current season at index `history.length` and assigns it chapter number `history.length + 1`. Each archived chapter uses its own id based on the stored identifier or its index. I'm also updating the page structure so the last "chapter" is actually the current season rather than a separate section.

I need to move the navigation into the render function itself since it depends on knowing how many archived items exist — it's hidden by default and only shown when there's more than one. The tables for champions and clubs always render based on the archived items, and the MVP showcase only appears if there are any MVPs to display. If a table would be empty, I should avoid rendering dead blocks. For the champions table, I need at least one archived item with a resolved champion, and the clubs table needs both archived data and at least one team with actual match history. I'm also thinking about whether the page should show the current season in the clubs table if it has a champion.

The current season's stats come from the live data, and I should only count teams excluded from the current season if they match the `Слот \d+` pattern to filter out placeholder slots. For chapter numbering, I'm using two-digit formatting with a minimum of 2 characters, so `pad2` handles that. The cover image alt text should be the tournament name or a photo caption, and for flat covers it's not needed. Gallery images use the caption if available, otherwise they get a generic alt description combining the tournament name with the photo number.

For the chapter navigation, I'm building scroll spy logic with a root margin that creates a cursor band in the middle of the viewport, checking if IntersectionObserver is available in the window before setting up the observer. Finalizing the chapter spy with proper guards for undefined window properties, then setting up the showcase for MVPs and the champion data table.

Writing component code...
Now the main script:

## Что сделано

**`history.html`** — переписан полностью:
- Шапка, бургер-меню и подвал скопированы из нового `index.html` (`#head`, `#burgerBtn`, `#menuPanel`, `#toTop`, `#headProgress`, `#year`), `aria-current="page"` — на «История».
- Никаких inline-скриптов; всё CSS — в `<style>` страницы (использованы классы из `site.css`, добавлены только специфичные для архива).
- Подключение: `ca-data.js` → `ca-ui.js` → `ca-views.js` → `ca-history.js`, все с `defer`.

**`assets/ca-history.js`** — новый, ES5 (`var`/`function`, без стрелок и шаблонных строк):
- Первый экран с фото последнего турнира и 4 агрегатами по всей истории (турниры / матчи / команды / действующий чемпион).
- «Текущий сезон» — всегда последняя глава (`#ch-now`): статус, прогресс `stats.played / matchesTotal`, состав, чемпион, кнопки на `/#bracket` и `/schedule.html`, аккуратное пустое состояние.
- Главы архива хронологически с обязательными якорями `id="ch-<id>"` (на них ссылается главная): обложка-фото или типографическая, чемпион + состав, финалист, MVP, «путь к титулу», галерея с лайтбоксом (←/→, Esc, свайп, счётчик).
- Сводные таблицы «Чемпионы турниров» и «Клубы и титулы» (титулы/финалы/матчи/карты по всем турнирам, прочерк вместо выдуманных данных), витрина MVP, липкая панель чипов с IntersectionObserver, JSON-LD `ItemList`.
- `load()` + `startAutoRefresh(60000)` + `onChange` с защитой от повторного рендера; после рендера переинициализируются reveal-наблюдатель, зум обложек, scroll-spy и галереи.

- Регресс `node .tmp-test\smoke.mjs` — 61 ok / 0 FAIL. **Итого 160 ok / 0 FAIL.**
